chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The pebbles of the Jamarah, if you take it from the Haram, it suffices you, and if you take it from other than the Haram, it does not suffice you.
He said, and he said: Do not pelt the Jamarah except with pebbles.

key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: The pebbles used for pelting the Jamarah
key_terms.يَجْزَأُ: To suffice/be valid for the ritual obligation

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of pebbles used in pelting the Jamarah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the ritual purity and validity of the Jamarah stones by linking their source to the sanctity of the Haram, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for ensuring the ritual's completeness. It further specifies the material constraint, mandating the use of small pebbles (hisa) rather than other objects, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of simplicity and adherence to the Sunnah during the stoning of the devil. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on both the physical attributes and the spiritual geography of Hajj rituals.
